body: ### Summary Overhauls the notification system to track unacted pending requests persistently, removes the "In Progress" status entirely, and removes the spinner arrows from the price input field. ### Problem The notification bell was showing all pending requests every time instead of only surfacing requests the admin hadn't acted on yet. There was no way to clear notifications, and the list didn't accumulate across sessions. The "In Progress" status added unnecessary complexity, and the number input's spin arrows cluttered the price field UI. ### Key Changes - **Unacted notifications hook (`useUnactedNotifications.ts`):** New custom hook that persists unacted notifications to local storage, tracks which requests have been opened/acted on, and exposes `addUnactedNotification`, `markAsActed`, and `clearAll` helpers. - **Notification accumulation:** New pending requests are automatically added to the unacted list; the list grows until the admin acts on a request or manually clears it. - **Mark as acted:** Opening a request detail (via notification click or inline edit) automatically removes it from the unacted notification list. - **Clear All button:** Added a "Clear All Notifications" button at the bottom of the notification modal so admins can dismiss the full list at once. - **Badge-only refresh:** Replaced the weekly full-page reload with a 15-second background poll (`refreshRequests`) that updates only the request list and notification badge without reloading the page. - **Removed "In Progress" status:** Dropped `"In Progress"` from the `ServiceRequest` type, status dropdowns, stats cards, and all status-based styling throughout the dashboard. - **Price input cleanup:** Added CSS to hide the native number input spin buttons (`-webkit-inner/outer-spin-button`) so users type a plain numeric value without arrow toggles. ---    --- To clone this PR locally use the [Github CLI](https://cli.github.com/) with command `gh pr checkout 32` You can tag me at @builderio for anything you want me to fix or change

body:
Currently, the `TelegramChannel` implementation fails with `ValueError: The parameter 'proxy' may only be set, if no request instance was set.` when a proxy is provided in the configuration. 

This is because the code attempts to set the proxy on the `ApplicationBuilder` while also providing a custom `HTTPXRequest` instance, which is not allowed in `python-telegram-bot`. 

This PR moves the proxy configuration directly into the `HTTPXRequest` initialization, resolving the startup crash.

## Pull Request description

Adds the missing C compiler toolchain to the dev environment so that
pre-commit hooks that compile C extensions (e.g. `djlint` depends on
the `regex` package) work out-of-the-box on a fresh Linux setup.

**Root cause:** pre-commit hook venvs are isolated and do not inherit the
conda PATH, so `gcc_linux-64` in conda alone was insufficient. System-level
`gcc` (via `build-essential`) is required.

Fixes #171

## How to test these changes

- `conda env create -f conda/dev.yaml && conda activate hiperhealth`
- `./scripts/install-dev.sh`
- `sudo apt install build-essential`
- `pre-commit run --all-files` — all hooks including `djlint` should pass

body:
## Summary

- **Reduce aaShift from 4 to 2** (Skia/tiny-skia default), expanding max coordinate range from ~2048px to 8191px
- aaShift=4 (16x AA) was unnecessarily aggressive — Skia ships aaShift=2 (4x AA) on billions of devices with excellent quality
- This is the root cause fix complementing PR #157 (path clipping + saturating arithmetic)

Follow-up to #148

## Details

At `aaShift=N`, both X and Y coordinates are scaled by `2^(N+6)` in `NewLineEdge`. This limits max pixel coordinate to `2^31 / 2^(N+6+10)` (after FDot6→FDot16 conversion):

| aaShift | Scale | Max Coord | Used by |
|---------|-------|-----------|---------|
| 2 | 256 | **8191px** | Skia, tiny-skia |
| 4 | 1024 | **~2047px** | gg (was) |

Skia's `SUPERSAMPLE_SHIFT=2` is the industry standard. When coordinates exceed the limit, Skia falls back to non-AA rendering rather than producing artifacts.

## Summary

Fixes the npm trusted publishing failure introduced in #174. The publish step was failing with `E404 Not Found` / `Access token expired or revoked`.

author: andymai
body:
## Summary

- **Fix hemisphere AABB bug**: face AABBs in `analytic_boolean()` were computed from wire vertices only. Hemisphere wires lie on the equator (z=0), producing flat-disk AABBs that missed face pairs above/below the equator. Replaced with `surface_aware_aabb()` that uses the actual surface extent for each surface type.
- **Fix chord explosion**: `sample_curve_clipped()` sampled intersection circles at 64 points, returning ~30 interior points as individual chord segments. `split_face()` is O(2^n) in chord count → exponential fragmentation. Replaced with `curve_boundary_crossings()` that finds entry/exit points where the curve crosses the face boundary (~2 chords instead of ~30).

### Benchmark results

| Benchmark | Before | After | Speedup |
|-----------|--------|-------|---------|
| `intersect(box,sphere) single` | 580 ms | **169 µs** | **3,432×** |
| `intersect(box,sphere) ×10` | ~5.8 s | **1.67 ms** | **~3,500×** |
| vs OCCT (86 ms) | 6.7× slower | **508× faster** | — |
